text:
Jack Quinn picked a good year to look like a first-line winger. He's in the last stretch before a new contract, and the Sabres have handed him 19 minutes a night (up from 15:39) and a seat on the ice for 79% of their power-play chances. He has answered with 19 points in 20 games, 0.95 a game against 0.62 last season.

The interesting part is that his luck runs both ways. He's shooting 16.1%, above his usual range, so his nine goals are a little ahead of his chances. But the Sabres have scored 5.9 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice, which has cost him assists. Net, the production looks sturdier than the shooting alone suggests. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking last season had 54% of his shots coming off the rush, and his EDGE skating speed sits in the 89th percentile, so he's a transition player through and through. The question mark is defensive: Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting noticeably more chances with him on the ice in 2025-26 (bottom 2% of forwards). That's the number Buffalo will be weighing when it talks money.
